newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish Permanent says buys Capital Home Loans.
newsitem.headline: Irish Permanent says buys Capital Home Loans.

text.p: Irish Permanent Plc said on Wednesday that it had acquired Capital Home Loans (CHL) Ltd, a wholly owned unit of Credit Foncier de France, for an undisclosed sum.
CHL, which has a current portfolio of residential mortgages in excess of 200 million sterling, is a first mortgage lender, Irish Permanent said in a statement.
It said it intends to amalgamate the existing UK mortgage operations of Irish Permanent with CHL to access a wider pool of mortgage intermediaries.

"The combination of Irish Permanent's product development expertise together with CHL's experience in the UK broker market and its distribution capabilities will position Irish Permanent to capitalise on the improving UK mortgage market," chief executive Roy Douglas said.
The combined mortgage portfolio in the UK will exceed 275 million sterling following the acquisition, Irish Permanent said.
CHL was set up in 1989 as a joint venture between Societe Generale and Credit Foncier de France (CFF). CFF, a French mortage and property lender, acquired 100 percent of CHL in 1992.
Irish Permanent converted from building society status to that of a public limited company and obtained a banking licence in 1994.
